name: Navy body fat
seoTitle: Navy body fat Calculator — Formula, Units & Example
seoDesc: Navy body fat: work out body fat (2) from the age and the height. A free health calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: Supply the age, the height, the neck circumference and the waist circumference and the Navy body fat calculator solves for body fat (2). Think of it as a shortcut for an informed starting point to take to a clinician, not a diagnosis. Every field is labelled the way you would say it out loud, so you can usually fill the form from memory and only look up the numbers you genuinely do not know.

sections.title: How does the Navy body fat calculator work?
sections.html:
The Navy body fat calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports body fat (2) in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the sex); then you type in the age, the height, the neck circumference and the waist circumference.

The arithmetic runs locally each time an input changes. The page knows which values you have given it and which it still has to derive, so the results panel is never stale.

sections.title: The formula behind the Navy body fat calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Body fat=450 × (-15456 × (height) + 19077 × (-neck circumference + waist circumference) + 6760) ÷ (15456 × (height) − 19077 × (-neck circumference + waist circumference) + 103240)
Body fat=450 × (-22100 × (height) + 35004 × (hip circumference − neck circumference + waist circumference) − 19579) ÷ (22100 × (height) − 35004 × (hip circumference − neck circumference + waist circumference) + 129579)
Result male=(age, sex, 450 × (-15456 × (height) + 19077 × (-neck circumference + waist circumference) + 6760) ÷ (15456 × (height) − 19077 × (-neck circumference + waist circumference) + 103240))
Result female=(age, sex, 450 × (-22100 × (height) + 35004 × (hip circumference − neck circumference + waist circumference) − 19579) ÷ (22100 × (height) − 35004 × (hip circumference − neck circumference + waist circumference) + 129579))

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

If a number looks wrong, check three things in this order: that the units match what you had in mind, that no drop-down is still on its default, and that the value you entered is on the same scale as the rest — a rate typed as 5 rather than 0.05 is the classic mistake. Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Every quantity with units carries a chip beside its box. Switching the chip does not change what you know, only how it is written: values are converted to a common internal base, the arithmetic happens there, and the answer is converted back for display. Mixing metres with feet in one calculation is therefore safe.

Results are rounded for display but computed at full precision, so chaining one result into the next does not accumulate error. Very large and very small numbers switch to scientific notation rather than printing a run of zeros.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Navy body fat calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Tracking a measurement over time and understanding what changed
  • Deciding whether a reading is worth a second look
  • Preparing for an appointment so you can describe your numbers clearly
  • Any time the same 4 figures keep coming back — the age, the height and the neck circumference — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Navy body fat calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns body fat (2), derived from the age, the height and the neck circumference. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Navy body fat calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the age, the height, the neck circumference and the waist circumference, which is 6 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter height in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Height opens in centimeters and the chip beside it offers 34 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There is one choice to make (1 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Body fat = -87. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Navy body fat calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
